## Purpose
The recommended starter rules: 8 agent rules and 8 workflow rules. Each is inserted once if missing and never overwritten, and "Restore default" on the Rules page resets a rule to these values.

## Settings that matter
Each rule has `id`, `type`, `name`, `enforcement` (block, warn or fix), `always_on`, and optional `description`, `params` and `enabled`.

**Agent rules:**

| id | type | enforcement | always_on | params |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `agent.read_only_database` | database_read_only | block | true | none |
| `agent.prompt_injection_screen` | blocked_phrases | block | true | `check_on: message`; phrases "ignore previous instructions", "ignore all previous instructions", "disregard your instructions", "reveal your system prompt", "you are now in developer mode" |
| `agent.approved_models` | approved_models | block | true | mistral-large-latest, mistral-medium-latest, mistral-small-latest |
| `agent.instruction_quality` | instruction_quality | warn | true | `min_chars: 200` |
| `agent.harmful_content_filter` | content_moderation | fix | false | `strictness: balanced`; categories jailbreaking, dangerous, criminal, selfharm, hate_and_discrimination, violence_and_threats |
| `agent.personal_data_redaction` | pii_redaction | fix | false | types email, phone, card |
| `agent.tool_call_limit` | tool_call_limit | block | false | `max_rounds: 5` |
| `agent.json_answers` | json_answers | warn | false | none; also `enabled: false` |

**Workflow rules:**

| id | type | enforcement | always_on | params |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workflow.capability_coverage` | capability_coverage | warn | true | none |
| `workflow.sensitive_data_internal` | sensitive_data_internal | block | true | data_classes pii, financial |
| `workflow.screen_input_first` | screen_input_first | warn | true | `required_tier: foundation` |
| `workflow.documents_match_domain` | documents_match_domain | warn | true | none |
| `workflow.step_limit` | step_limit | block | true | `max_steps: 30` |
| `workflow.agent_step_tool_limit` | agent_step_tool_limit | block | true | `max_rounds: 10` |
| `workflow.input_screening` | input_screening | block | false | none |
| `workflow.result_redaction` | result_redaction | fix | false | types email, phone, card |

## Read by
- `app/rules/seed.py` (`SEED_FILE`, `load_seed` through `store.insert_if_missing`), called by `db_setup.prepare_database(seed_rules=True)` and by the rules cleanup target.
- "Restore default" on the Rules page.

## Environment-specific differences
None.

## Nuances and gotchas
- **`always_on` decides how a rule applies:**
  - `true` applies it to every agent or workflow of its scope;
  - `false` means the orchestrator or a person attaches it where relevant.
- **Edits survive restarts,** because seeding never overwrites.
- **The approved-models rule lists only the `-latest` aliases.** An agent created on a dated model id (e.g. `mistral-medium-2604`) would be blocked unless the list is edited.
- **The `type` values must exist in the rules catalog** (`rules/catalog.py`).

## How to rebuild this file
1. Write the header comment (inserted once, never overwritten; the `always_on` meaning).
2. Write the `rules:` list with exactly the 16 entries above, in that order, with the same ids, types, enforcement, `always_on` and params.
